messages:
maya: FYI customer 238 opened an escalation — SDK estimator shows ~12.3k tokens but invoice = 15.1k. They provided a repro and say nothing changed on their end. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

billing-bot: invoice snapshot attached — invoice_id=inv_2026_238, period=2026-03, total_tokens_reported=15101

alex: can you paste the request payload + sdk version? also need request_id if available.

maya: SDK version 0.9.2. request_id=01F8ZQ9X. quick repro (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant\u0000\u0000\u0000"},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this..."}], "request_id":"01F8ZQ9X" }'
```
Note the system message has trailing null bytes — customer says their app serializes a legacy C lib that pads strings.

simon: interesting. client-side estimator probably normalizes out control chars; server tokenizer might treat nulls as tokens or change normalization. we should verify token counts with our tokenizer and the estimator library.

priya: grabbing metering logs for request_id=01F8ZQ9X now. stand by.

ingest-bot: metering log: request=01F8ZQ9X server_count=15101 model=rwd-small route=hosted-prod ts=1764509892

alex: try running the same payload through the SDK estimator locally (same version) and also run our server tokenizer on the raw bytes. share outputs.

maya: ran local estimator (sdk 0.9.2) — returns 12234 tokens. ran server tokenizer against raw request body -> 15101 tokens.

simon: that delta is consistent with control-char handling or extra server-side prefills. do we inject any hidden system/tool messages for diagnostics?

alex: checking apply-inject pipeline... found an injected step: `kv_cache_prefill` that adds a diagnostic span to completions for some resumed sessions. it added ~120 tokens for this request (seen in runtime trace). but that doesn't explain 2.9k tokens.

priya: grep of audit log for 01F8ZQ9X shows additional server-side metadata blocks appended before tokenization: `__internal:pgp_padding:<base64...>` — seems like a base64 blob with null padding landed in the message body.

maya: the customer's repro includes a base64-encoded attachment in a different call path that the SDK serializes as `attachment_b64` with NUL padding for block alignment. SDK estimator currently strips NULs in its tokenizer path for speed. server tokenizer does not.

simon: aha. Base64 padded with NUL bytes -> when decoded server sees extra zero bytes and our Unicode-normalization path tokenizes them. the client estimator's pre-tokenization normalization strips `\u0000` when computing estimates. mismatch source found.

alex: short-term mitigation: 1) billing: flag invoice inv_2026_238 for review/credit if we decide to exclude NUL-only token overhead, 2) eng: quick server-side normalization to remove trailing NULs from text fields before token counting, 3) sdk: update estimator to mimic server normalization so counts match. owners?

priya: I'll open billing ticket. assign to @maya for customer comms.

maya: assigned. I'll propose a provisional credit while we confirm exact token delta.

alex: engineering will patch runtime normalization. I'll take the server-side change (hotfix) and add tests. estimate 3-4 hrs.

simon: I'll add a unit test to tokenizer comparing server vs sdk normalization and add a regression test for base64->decoded null padding.

maya: customer also worried about hidden tool/system messages adding tokens. to be clear, server only added `kv_cache_prefill` (120 tokens) + the null-padding delta (~2850 tokens). total explains invoice.

ingest-bot: meter-recalc: request=01F8ZQ9X server_raw_count=15101 server_normalized_count=12231 (post-normalization simulation)

priya: billing note: tentative credit = invoice_tokens - normalized_tokens => 2870 tokens credit. CC finance.

alex: follow-ups: - PR for runtime normalization (me) - SDK patch to mirror normalization and release patch 0.9.3 (simon) - postmortem + docs update on how padding affects token counts (maya+priya) - billing credit action (maya)

maya: I'll draft a short note to the customer explaining root cause (legacy client padding + tokenizer normalization mismatch) and next steps.

simon: tiny repro snippet to validate locally (python):
```py
# decode base64 attachment with possible NUL padding then run tokenizer
raw = base64.b64decode(attachment_b64)
# server normalization (what we will enforce): raw = raw.rstrip(b"\x00")
# then decode to text and tokenize
```

maya: thanks all. will update customer once billing confirms. :thumbsup:

alex: marking this thread for follow-up in 72h. if billing done earlier ping here. :clock3:

priya: closing loop with finance now.

maya: resolved for now — saving logs under /support/escalations/01F8ZQ9X and will file postmortem after SDK patch.
